first_impression.reaction: Honestly expected another listicle with the 'vein of love' line copied from Pinterest. Instead the intro says 'Some of these are history. Many are not.' and promises to flag the stories that don't hold up. That's the tone I want. It doesn't gush, so I kept going, skimming the headings and the 'Our view' lines.

journey.quote: This guide sets out where each tradition really comes from, using museum, encyclopaedia and church sources, and flags the stories that do not hold up.
journey.reaction: Good. As a lawyer I like seeing where the claims come from. It makes this feel more Condé Nast than wedding forum.

journey.quote: If your celebrant will explain a ritual to 80 guests, the explanation should be true.
journey.reaction: This is exactly my fear about looking try-hard in front of our friends. It's a sharp line and James would like it too.

journey.quote: So many couples complete the legal marriage at home and give the ceremony abroad all the meaning. Your Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements for your destination.
journey.reaction: This is the bit that actually matters to us. Legal at home, symbolic overseas is a clear, honest trade-off. I'd want a bit more on what that looks like for Italy specifically, but the direction is reassuring.

journey.quote: At a venue abroad, agree in advance who supplies the glass and its cloth or bag, who clears up, and whether breaking glass is allowed on a terrace or lawn.
journey.reaction: Not our tradition, but this is the kind of insider detail that tells me someone has actually run these weddings. Same with the open-flame rules for the Hindu fire. That's what separates a planner from a blog.

journey.quote: Venue rules on paper confetti, rice and petals vary and are rarely published, so your Wedded Advisor confirms what is allowed in writing before you order anything.
journey.reaction: 'In writing' is the right phrase for me. That's accountability, which is my main worry.

journey.quote: At a multi-day wedding, move some speeches to the welcome dinner so the wedding night runs to time.
journey.reaction: Practical and probably what we'll do. Nice to see the multi-day weekend treated as normal.

journey.quote: customs vary by region, so ask your planner what is kept where you marry.
journey.reaction: Italy is high on our list and this section is the thinnest one. Almonds and bomboniere I already knew. It just points me to two other articles. I wanted one regional detail I hadn't seen before.

journey.quote: Through [Wonderland Concierge](/wonderland-concierge), one Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, start to finish.
journey.reaction: 'One Wedded Advisor' is what I want to hear, since I don't want things passed to strangers. But 'start to finish' is what every planner says. What does it actually include? Also, everywhere else it's Wedded this and Wedded that, and here it's 'Wonderland Concierge'. Is that a different service?

journey.section: How to choose which traditions to keep
journey.quote: The best ceremonies rarely keep every tradition, only the few the couple and their families would genuinely miss.
journey.reaction: The table is the bit I'd screenshot and send to Mum. Clean and decisive.

unanswered_questions: What does the Wedded Advisor's 'start to finish' actually cover? Does it include guest flights and airport transfers for older guests?
Is 'Wonderland Concierge' the same as the Wedded Advisor service, or something separate?
For a legal ceremony in Sydney and a symbolic one in Italy, does the Advisor help with the Australian side, or only the overseas one?
Is there a real wedding you've planned where a couple blended traditions like this, with venue and date, that I can look at?

turn_offs_found.quote: a Wedded Advisor will plan it with you from first idea to the last dance.
turn_offs_found.why: Not a deal-breaker, but 'first idea to the last dance' leans towards the wedding-brochure language the rest of the article avoids so well. It's the one line that sounds like marketing.

would_share_with: Mum, for the giving-away section and the 'both families answer' option

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk through a ceremony that blends your family's traditions with the customs of your destination, a Wedded Advisor will plan it with you from first idea to the last dance.
cta_reaction.why: It isn't pushy, which I appreciate, and 'when you are ready' fits where we are. But this is an educational piece and we're 14 months out with no destination. I'd bookmark the brand and read a couple more posts and a real wedding before enquiring. That's our normal process, not a flaw in the page.

top_3_changes: In the mid-article CTA, say concretely what 'start to finish' includes (e.g. guest travel and transfers), and make the service name match the rest of the brand language so it doesn't read as a separate product.
Give the Italy section one specific, insider regional detail rather than only linking out, since it's the destination most readers like us are weighing up.
Swap 'from first idea to the last dance' in the closing CTA for something as plain and specific as the rest of the article.
